reviewedChanges.reason: requestLocal now binds its receipt event ID to requestHash, parentAttempt and messages, so successive rejected actions at the same uncreated operation slot have distinct request receipts. The public operationId/requestHash/session and workspace lease ownership remain unchanged. The finite LocalEffects initial prefix submits one original and one competitor action in separate works, and HostRetry submits two distinct first/second argv actions; neither graph generates a rejected repeat-limit request. Existing Duplicate actions replay their saved exact event bodies or host retry request identity, so their at-most-once semantics remain in the retained driver.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: LOCAL_REQUEST adds a guard rejecting a third identical diagnosable CLI failure for ordinary members, before any operation is created. LocalEffects has one original operation and a contender in another work, with no further CLI request in its graph. HostRetry source receipts have distinct argv and no diagnosable stderr; successors are host batch operations. No third same-key diagnosable request is reachable in these slices. LOCAL_RESULT/RECONCILE, finishOperation/checkpoint consumption, uncertain effects, session matching, recovery and leases are unchanged. New repeat-limiting semantics are covered by BT_L121 and the real XState gate, not inferred from these old graphs.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice

promise: Existing unknown-effects, receipt/checkpoint/lease atomicity and host-batch retirement promises are unchanged. New tool recommendation and repeat-limiting semantics are accepted by separate BDD/XState tests, not added to the old finite domains.
limitations: No proof of natural-language tool choice, arbitrary CLI histories, arbitrary metadata/repeat failures combined with host effects, infinite failures, OS isolation or external service exactly-once effects.
